newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong home mortgage lending up in September.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong home mortgage lending up in September.

text.p: Home mortgage lending in Hong Kong grew by one percent in September, a moderate increase from the August figure of 0.8 percent, the Hong Kong Monetary Association (HKMA) said on Friday.
The latest HKMA monthly survey showed the total amount of outstanding mortgage lending by the 33 institutions polled increased to HK$307.8 billion.
The growth rate was lower than the monthly average of 1.3 percent over the last 12 months, the HKMA said.

"As expected, the growth of of residential mortgage lending picked up during the month given the increased activity in the property market in August, said David Carse, deputy chief executive of the HKMA.
The annualized rate of growth in lending over the last three months decreased to 12.8 percent from 14.3 percent in the three-month period to August, the report said.
The 12-month average of outstanding loans showed an annualized growth rate of 15.5 percent, compared with 16.2 percent in August.
The amount of new loans approved but not yet drawn rose by HK$1.9 billion, or 22.9 percent, to HK$10 billion in September.
"Judging from these figures and the sustained trading activity in the property market in September, the growth rate of outstanding loans is likely to be higher in October," Carse said in a statement.
Lending for the purchase of properties in China increased by 0.7 percent to HK$5.9 billion in September.
Gross loans made in September decreased in number, to 214 from 346, and in amount to HK$133 million from HK$165 million.
New loans approved in September decreased in number to 316 from 338, but increased in amount to HK$308 million from HK$238 million.
